alternatives: The TAR is mislabeled: the package may actually be an ORDENCP4 runtime/package while project.cfg retained or was incorrectly set to ORDENCP1.
The TAR is multi-controller/shared: ORDENCP1 is the project/runtime identity, ORDENCP4 rows are a secondary-controller or foreign subset, and N/A Conveyor rows require another ownership rule.
The Conveyor Machine_Name field is not authoritative for all conveyor records; N/A may mean globally shared/unscoped rather than belonging to either controller.
why_alternatives_rejected: TAR-mislabeled is not proven because the filename, device/logical/claimed identity, and project.cfg all independently indicate ORDENCP1.
Multi-controller ownership is plausible but not proven because no supplied controller map, endpoint configuration, or asset-reference analysis assigns the N/A rows or explains the ORDENCP4 subset.
Treating N/A as ORDENCP1 is rejected because no evidence states that N/A inherits project.cfg MACHINENAME, and that assumption would bypass the observed filter failure.
ai.recommended_action: Keep the package identity as ORDENCP1 for remediation tracking, but do not import/filter N/A Conveyor rows as ORDENCP1 and do not declare an actual physical controller. Quarantine the 469 explicit ORDENCP4 rows as foreign pending validation. Escalate for deterministic ownership resolution using the listed checks; if validators establish an inheritance/shared-row rule for N/A rows, apply that rule explicitly and re-run import. If they instead establish that ORDENCP4 owns the runtime assets, correct the package/project identity as a mislabeled TAR.
